story.overview:
As a Slack user, I want to upload files (PDFs, images, CSV, text) in my message to Orion, so that Claude can read, analyze, and reference the file content in its response.
When users upload files to Slack messages addressed to Orion, the files are ingested into Claude's context. This enables document analysis, data extraction, image understanding, and file-based Q&A. The implementation downloads files from Slack (authenticated), uploads to Anthropic Files API, and includes as document blocks in the Claude request.
FR51: System ingests files uploaded in Slack messages - downloads via Slack API, uploads to Anthropic Files API, includes as document blocks in Claude context.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Given a message with attached files, When the handler processes the message, Then the files array in the event is detected
Given multiple files in a single message, When files are ingested, Then all files are processed (batch operation)
Given a message with files, When files are detected, Then a log entry is created with file count, names, and sizes
Given a Slack file URL, When download is requested, Then the content is fetched from url_private_download
Given a download request, When authentication is needed, Then the Slack bot token is used in Authorization header
Given a download failure, When the error is caught, Then a user-friendly message is returned (not a crash)
Given a file size validation, When the file exceeds limits, Then download is rejected with size limit error
Given a downloaded file buffer, When upload is requested, Then the buffer is uploaded to Anthropic Files API
Given upload implementation, When code is written, Then existing FilesApiClient is reused (not duplicated)
Given upload success/failure, When the operation completes, Then outcome is tracked in Langfuse
Given a successful upload, When the file ID is returned, Then a document block is created with source.type: file and file_id
Given a document block with file, When Citations (Story 8.1) is enabled, Then citations: { enabled: true } is included
Given file ingestion results, When passed to agent loop, Then buildDocumentBlocks() adds them to messages array
Given an unsupported file type, When validation runs, Then clear error message lists supported formats
Given a PDF file, When size is checked, Then max 100MB is enforced
Given an image file, When size is checked, Then max 20MB is enforced
Given a CSV file, When size is checked, Then max 100MB is enforced
Given a text file (.txt, .md, .json), When size is checked, Then max 100MB is enforced
Given unsupported file type, When error is shown, Then supported formats are listed: PDF, PNG, JPG, GIF, CSV, TXT, MD, JSON, XML, YAML
Given a file too large, When error is shown, Then message includes actual size and limit
Given download failure, When error is shown, Then message suggests retry or smaller file
Given the file ingestion flow, When complete, Then full pipeline works: Slack -> download -> upload -> document block -> Claude

dependencies.dependency: Story 8.1 - Citations API (integration for document citations)

technical-notes.note: Pipeline: Slack Message -> Handler Detection -> ingestSlackFiles() -> downloadSlackFile() -> FilesApiClient.uploadBuffer() -> buildDocumentBlocks() -> Agent Loop (Claude receives documents)
FILE_TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_TYPE, DOWNLOAD_FAILED, UPLOAD_FAILED, ZERO_BYTE_FILE, FILE_EXPIRED
Never throws - returns FileIngestionResult with error
Uses logger.* with traceId, never console.log

relevant-sections.section: Epic 8 Story 8.3 (FR51) - Slack File Ingestion for Claude Context. Allow users to upload files in Slack that Claude can read and analyze.

Flow: Detect files in Slack message -> Download from Slack (url_private_download with Authorization header) -> Upload to Anthropic Files API (reuse Story 6.5 client) -> Include as document block with file_id -> Claude reads and analyzes file content with Citations (Story 8.1)
Files API Client location: src/files/api-client.ts Operations: getFile(fileId) -> Download, getFileMetadata(fileId) -> Fetch info Supports: xlsx, pdf, docx, pptx, png, jpg, svg, csv, json, txt
